skill.description: Security operations template kit for creating AppSec, DevSecOps, compliance, incident response, and secure SDLC workflows. It provides a concise SKILL.md pattern, workflow checklist, security rule template, CI scanning template, and remediation examples. Use when: designing a new security skill, documenting SAST or secrets workflows, mapping findings to OWASP, CWE, or MITRE ATT&CK, or building reusable security review guidance.
skill.summary: Template kit for building security operations AI skills and secure SDLC workflows.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, defensive security examples, and standards reference links. I confirmed the CI template remote pipe-to-shell installer and GITHUB_TOKEN exposure to a third-party action as publish-relevant risks; no prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-bash tfsec install with a pinned action or pinned release download, and verify checksums before execution.

remediation.issue: The Gitleaks action receives GITHUB_TOKEN from repository secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Define least-privilege workflow permissions, pin the action to an immutable commit, and pass only the token scope required.

remediation.issue: The published skill still contains placeholder metadata and example.com links.
remediation.suggestion: Replace all placeholder descriptions, categories, maintainers, and reference links with accurate project-specific content before publication.

content.value_statement: Security teams often repeat the same workflow, rule, and CI guidance across projects. This skill provides templates for SecOps skills, detection rules, checklists, and CI security scans.
actual_capabilities: Provides a SKILL.md structure for security operations workflows.
Includes checklist patterns for sequential, conditional, iterative, and incident response work.
Supplies a CI template for SAST, dependency, secrets, container, and IaC scans.
Includes a security rule template with OWASP, CWE, and compliance metadata.
Provides remediation examples for SQL injection, XSS, API auth, password hashing, and file uploads.
limitations: It is a template kit, not a complete production security program.
The CI template needs review before use because it downloads tools and uses GitHub Actions secrets.
Example rules and code must be adapted to actual languages, frameworks, and policies.
It does not replace expert review for incident response or compliance decisions.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI security checks

use_cases.title: Document remediation playbooks
use_cases.description: Turn common vulnerability guidance into clear rules, examples, checklists, and reporting language.

prompt_templates.title: Start a security skill

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI security workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the CI security template for a Node and Python repository. Include dependency, secrets, SAST, container, and IaC checks.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a detection rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate rule authoring for AppSec teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security rule for unsafe HTML rendering. Include severity, confidence, references, remediation guidance, and test examples.

prompt_templates.title: Build an incident workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design for security operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incident response checklist for suspected credential exposure. Include triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and reporting steps.

output_examples.input: Create a rule for SQL injection review.
output: Rule goal: detect string-built SQL queries that include user input.
Severity: high, because exploitation can expose or modify database records.
Remediation: use parameterized queries or a safe ORM pattern.

output_examples.input: Prepare a CI security workflow for a service repository.
output: Workflow stages: source checkout, dependency scan, SAST, secret detection, container scan, and report upload.
Failure policy: block critical dependency findings and record other findings for review.
Security note: pin actions, verify downloaded tools, and use least-privilege tokens.

output_examples.input: Summarize a remediation checklist for exposed credentials.
output: Triage: identify affected secrets, repositories, services, and logs.
Containment: revoke exposed values and rotate dependent credentials.
Recovery: validate access, scan history, and document the incident timeline.

best_practices: Replace all placeholders before publishing a derived security skill.
Pin external actions and installers before using generated CI templates.
Keep vulnerable examples clearly labeled and separate from production-ready guidance.
anti_patterns: Publish this template without replacing placeholder metadata and links.
Run remote installer commands from the CI template without pinning and verification.
Treat example vulnerable snippets as production-safe code.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create security operations skill templates, workflow checklists, detection rules, and CI scanning guidance.

faq.question: Is this a scanner?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and guidance. Tools in generated CI workflows perform the scanning.

faq.question: Can I use the CI template directly?
faq.answer: Review it first. Pin actions, verify installers, and adjust permissions before running it in a repository.

faq.question: Which standards does it reference?
faq.answer: It references OWASP, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, SOC 2, GDPR, and PCI DSS.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It teaches secret detection and safe secret handling, but it does not manage secrets for you.

faq.question: Is it safe for production?
faq.answer: Use it as a starting point. Replace placeholders and complete security review before production use.
